subject: microbiology
title: Systemic and opportunistic mycoses

steps.tx: Aspergillus fumigatus grows septate hyphae with **acute angle branching** and fruiting bodies in cavities, and disease follows immunity. Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis complicates asthma with fleeting shadows, high IgE and central bronchiectasis, treated with steroids and itraconazole. **Aspergilloma** balls fungus in old TB cavities with haemoptysis and air crescent, needing resection or embolisation. Invasive aspergillosis strikes neutropenia with halo sign nodules and positive galactomannan, answered by **voriconazole** first line. Culture with KOH and biopsy proves, and septate versus broad aseptate splits therapy instantly.
steps.say: Aspergillus is separated from mucor at the microscope. Its hyphae carry septa and branch at acute angles with fruiting bodies, which is the morphology to memorise. Allergy produces fleeting shadows with high IgE in asthmatics, a fungus ball bleeds from an old cavity with an air crescent, and invasion strikes neutropenic lungs with halo nodules. Galactomannan is the blood marker of invasion, voriconazole is the drug of choice, and the septate versus aseptate divide is the fork that decides therapy.

vis.caption: Aspergillus fumigatus: microscopy, aspergilloma (air crescent), and invasive aspergillosis (halo sign)

steps.tx: Mucormycosis grows broad **aseptate hyphae with right angle branching**, with Rhizopus thriving in **diabetic ketoacidosis** and post COVID steroid lungs. It invades vessels with tissue necrosis: **rhino orbital cerebral** disease with black turbinate, facial pain, ophthalmoplegia and cavernous thrombosis, plus pulmonary and cutaneous forms. Management is **liposomal amphotericin B** with urgent surgical debridement and sugar control, stepping down to posaconazole or isavuconazole. Voriconazole fails mucor and must never substitute, and biopsy with frozen section decides within hours.
steps.say: Mucor is the emergency that eats vessels. Broad hyphae without septa branch at right angles and invade arterial walls, which is the angioinvasion behind black necrotic tissue. Diabetic ketoacidosis and steroid treated COVID are the settings, and rhino orbital cerebral disease announces itself with facial pain, eye signs and a black turbinate. Liposomal amphotericin with urgent surgical debridement and sugar control is the treatment, voriconazole is useless here, and frozen section biopsy is the test that decides within hours.

steps.tx: The silver stain convicts mucor in one glance. Broad **aseptate hyphae** without cross walls snake across the field and fork with **right angle branching**, unlike the acute angles of Aspergillus. Several hyphae pierce an arterial wall, the **angioinvasion** that infarcts tissue black. This is diabetic ketoacidosis or steroid suppressed lung rendered in pathology, and the exam expects liposomal amphotericin with urgent debridement, never voriconazole.
steps.say: Look at this stain for three labels. The black ribbons have no cross walls, which is what aseptate means, and they fork at right angles, which is how mucor differs from Aspergillus. The third label is the darkest: hyphae bored straight through an arterial wall, which is angioinvasion that starves tissue of blood. This is the pathology behind black turbinates and infarcted lungs in ketoacidosis, which is why treatment is amphotericin with the knife, never voriconazole.

vis.alt: Silver stained tissue showing broad aseptate hyphae with right angle branching invading an arterial wall.
vis.caption: Histology showing aseptate hyphae with right angle branching and angioinvasion. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Candida albicans forms pseudohyphae with **germ tubes** and chlamydospores, then invades lines and guts. **Oesophageal candidiasis** in AIDS brings dysphagia with white plaques that bleed on scrape, answered by fluconazole, as does vulvovaginitis in diabetes. Candidaemia from TPN and broad antibiotics demands line removal with echinocandin then step down, plus fundoscopy and echo for seeding. Cryptococcus neoformans is a capsulated budding yeast from pigeon droppings showing India ink halos, causing **cryptococcal meningitis** in AIDS with high pressure headache, diagnosed by CrAg lateral flow and induced with amphotericin plus flucytosine.
steps.say: Candida and Cryptococcus are the yeasts to contrast. Candida forms germ tubes and invades lines and oesophagus when immunity or flora fails, and white plaques that bleed on scraping with dysphagia mean oesophagitis that fluconazole cures. Bloodstream infection follows parenteral nutrition and broad antibiotics, and lines must come out with echinocandin therapy and eye and heart checks. Cryptococcus is the capsulated yeast from pigeon droppings that causes meningitis with raised pressure headache in AIDS, which is diagnosed by CrAg lateral flow and induced with amphotericin plus flucytosine.

steps.tx: **Pneumocystis jirovecii** fills alveoli with cysts, showing ground glass with pneumatoceles once CD4 falls below 200, with exertional desaturation and raised LDH. **TMP-SMX** treats and prevents, with steroids added in hypoxia. **Dimorphics** are mould in soil and yeast in tissue: Histoplasma of Ohio Mississippi bat caves with calcified nodes answered by itraconazole, Coccidioides of desert Southwest with spherules and endospores plus erythema nodosum, Blastomyces with broad based budding in skin and prostate, Paracoccidioides with pilot wheel in Latin America, and Talaromyces marneffei with umbilicated papules in Southeast Asian AIDS.
steps.say: Pneumocystis is the pneumonia of low CD4 counts. Ground glass lungs with pneumatoceles and desaturation on exertion below a CD4 of two hundred point to it, and cotrimoxazole both treats and prevents with steroids added in hypoxia. Dimorphic fungi switch shape with temperature, growing as mould in soil and yeast in tissue. Histoplasma follows bat caves, Coccidioides follows deserts with red nodules on shins, Blastomyces buds broadly in skin and prostate, Paracoccidioides shows a pilot wheel, and Talaromyces dots Southeast Asian AIDS patients with umbilicated papules.
